proposals.before: Emperor Dezong ordered a general assault; Na's clansman Li Wei defected with Xuzhou, while Li Shizhen surrendered Dezhou and Li Changqing Di Prefecture. Furious at Wei's betrayal and mindful of Xuzhou's rugged defenses, Na threw his entire army against him.
proposals.after: Emperor Dezong ordered a general assault; Na's clansman Li Wei defected with Xuzhou, while Li Shizhen surrendered Dezhou and Li Changqing surrendered Di Prefecture. Furious at Wei's betrayal and mindful of Xuzhou's rugged defenses, Na threw his entire army against him.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits the verb for Li Changqing, fusing his name with Di Prefecture into an ungrammatical phrase.

proposals.before: The emperor sent the Xuanwu and Liu Xuanzuo commands to relieve Xuzhou and inflicted a crushing defeat on Na's army.
proposals.after: The emperor ordered the Xuanwu army and Liu Xuanzuo to direct the relief and inflicted a crushing defeat on Na's army.
proposals.reason: Chinese pairs the Xuanwu command with Liu Xuanzuo as the directing force; the idiomatic English treats Xuanwu as if it were a parallel personal command name.

proposals.before: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, he, together with Du You and Li Luan, all obtained to ennoble concubines by state as ladies; he was advanced to co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
proposals.after: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, he, together with Du You and Li Luan, all obtained the privilege of ennobling concubines as state ladies; he was advanced to co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
proposals.reason: The literal English is ungrammatical ('obtained to ennoble' / 'by state as ladies') and obscures the privilege of conferring state-lady titles on concubines.

proposals.before: He was promoted through acting Minister of Works to honorary Grand Councillor, then Grand Mentor and Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, and enfeoffed as Prince of Raoyang.
proposals.after: He rose through acting Minister of Works, was added as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, served as Grand Mentor while also Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Raoyang commandery.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic version collapses 同中書門下平章事 and misjoins 司徒兼太子太保 as if both titles were of the Crown Prince.

proposals.before: When he heard that Li Guangyan had taken the Lingyun stockade, he was greatly afraid for the first time, sent envoys to submit, and the emperor, heavily dividing troops to meet two enemies, therefore ordered the attendant censor Liu Gongchuo to console him and added acting Minister of Works.
proposals.after: When he heard that Li Guangyan had taken the Lingyun stockade, he was greatly afraid for the first time, sent envoys to submit, and the emperor, heavily dividing troops to meet two enemies, therefore ordered the Supervising Secretary Liu Gongchuo to console him and added acting Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is Supervising Secretary (Attendant Gentleman), not 'attendant censor'; the literal office title is mistranslated.

proposals.before: His household women and old nurses clamored, "Your forefathers' lands—how can you surrender them in a day?
proposals.after: His household women and old nurses clamored, "The former Grand Mentor's lands—how can you surrender them in a day?
proposals.reason: 先司徒 denotes a specific former Grand Mentor, not an undifferentiated 'forefathers'; the idiomatic plural invents a different referent.

proposals.before: Their bodies lay unclaimed until a cultivated gentleman gave them burial outside the west gate.
proposals.after: Their bodies lay unclaimed until the gentleman Yingxiu gave them burial outside the west gate.
proposals.reason: Chinese 有士英秀 names the gentleman Yingxiu; the idiomatic English drops the personal name.

proposals.before: Their corpses were abandoned; none dared to attend them; a refined gentleman buried them outside the left of the city.
proposals.after: Their corpses were abandoned; none dared to attend them; a refined gentleman, Yingxiu, buried them outside the left of the city.
proposals.reason: Chinese 士英秀 is the personal name Yingxiu, omitted in the literal English.

proposals.before: Wang Chengqing, a favored commander and brother-in-law through Shidao's niece, had plotted with his men to arrest Shidao during maneuvers; when Wu stormed the city he fled to Xuzhou and defected to the court.
proposals.after: Wang Chengqing, a favored commander and younger brother of Chengzong, whom Shidao had married to his elder brother's daughter, had plotted with his men to arrest Shidao during maneuvers; when Wu stormed the city he fled to Xuzhou and defected to the court.
proposals.reason: Chinese 承宗弟也 names Chengzong as elder brother; the idiomatic English omits Chengzong and wrongly calls Chengqing Shidao's brother-in-law.

proposals.before: His aide Li Yumou urged, "The siege drags on and Yiwu's army never comes.
proposals.after: His aide Li Yu urged, "The siege drags on and Yiwu's army never comes.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李宇謀曰 is the name 李宇 plus the verb 謀; fusing 謀 into Yumou invents a wrong personal name.

proposals.before: The staff officer Li Yumou said: "The city has been long besieged and the circuit troops do not come to our aid.
proposals.after: The staff officer Li Yu advised, saying: "The city has been long besieged and the circuit troops do not come to our aid.
proposals.reason: 謀 is the verb advised/planned, not part of the name 李宇.

proposals.before: The court ordered Cang to send Yiwu twelve hundred thousand strings in cash and tens of thousands of bushels of grain yearly, with Yu as his chief aide.
proposals.after: The court ordered Cang to send Yiwu one hundred twenty thousand strings in cash and tens of thousands of bushels of grain yearly, with Yu as his chief aide.
proposals.reason: 十二萬 is 120,000; twelve hundred thousand wrongly multiplies the figure by ten.

proposals.before: In the sixteenth year Huaizhi died and was posthumously honored as Grand Protector General of Yangzhou.
proposals.after: In the sixteenth year Huaizhi died and was posthumously honored as Grand Governor-General of Yangzhou.
proposals.reason: 大都督 denotes Grand Governor-General (dudu), not Protector General (都護).

proposals.before: Li Quanlüe, of the Li-Wang clan, born Rijian, had served Wang Wujun as a junior officer.
proposals.after: Li Quanlüe, of the Li-Wang clan, named Rijian, had served Wang Wujun as a junior officer.
proposals.reason: 名日簡 means he was named Rijian, not born Rijian.

proposals.before: The court stripped his titles and ordered Wu Chongyin to lead Yan and Qi forces against him.
proposals.after: The court stripped his titles and ordered Wu Chongyin to lead Yun and Qi forces against him.
proposals.reason: 鄆 is Yun Prefecture, not Yan; the idiomatic English misidentifies the place.

proposals.before: Tongxun and the others, because they were born of a different mother, were lent death by pardon and were allowed to follow their mother to the place of exile, it is said.
proposals.after: Tongxun and the others, because they were born of a different mother, were spared death by a grant of clemency and were allowed to follow their mother to the place of exile, it is said.
proposals.reason: 貸死 means commutation of the death penalty; 'lent death by pardon' is an unnatural calque.

decisions.reason: Chinese 李士真以德州、李長卿以棣州送款 parallels both officers offering surrender; the idiomatic drops the verb before Di Prefecture and leaves an ungrammatical fusion, which the repair restores.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李士真以德州、李長卿以棣州送款

decisions.reason: 帝命宣武、劉玄佐督諸軍進援 pairs the Xuanwu army with the person Liu Xuanzuo as joint directors of the relief; calling both 'commands' misreads 劉玄佐, and the repair correctly separates army and person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝命宣武、劉玄佐督諸軍進援

decisions.reason: 皆得封妾媵以國為夫人 is the privilege of ennobling concubines as state ladies; the literal's 'obtained to ennoble' / 'by state as ladies' is ungrammatical and obscure, and the repair restores the sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皆得封妾媵以國為夫人

decisions.reason: 加同中書門下平章事 is a distinct office, and 以司徒兼太子太保 makes 司徒 concurrent with 太子太保; the idiomatic collapses the former and can attach 'of the Crown Prince' to both titles, while the repair keeps the offices distinct and adds 郡 to Raoyang.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加同中書門下平章事，以司徒兼太子太保，封饒陽郡王

decisions.reason: 給事中 is the Supervising Secretary post, not an attendant censor (侍御史-type title); the literal mistranslates the office, and Supervising Secretary is the correct repair.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 命給事中柳公綽慰撫之

decisions.reason: 先司徒土地 refers to the late Grand Mentor's lands as a specific titled person, not plural forefathers; the idiomatic invents the wrong referent, and the repair restores it.
有士英秀 names the gentleman Yingxiu who performed the burial; the idiomatic omits that personal name, and restoring Yingxiu matches the Chinese.
The literal likewise drops 英秀 after 士; inserting Yingxiu as the gentleman's name restores the named agent without changing the rest.

承宗弟也 identifies Chengqing as Chengzong's younger brother, and 師道以兄女妻之 is Shidao marrying him to his elder brother's daughter; the idiomatic omits Chengzong and mislabels the kinship as brother-in-law, which the repair corrects.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 親將王承慶，承宗弟也，師道以兄女妻之

decisions.reason: 李宇謀曰 is the personal name 李宇 plus the verb 謀; fusing 謀 into Yumou invents a false name, and Li Yu is the correct repair.
The literal also treats 謀 as part of the name; rendering 李宇 with 謀 as advised/said correctly separates name and verb.
錢十二萬緡 is 120,000 strings; 'twelve hundred thousand' multiplies the figure tenfold, and one hundred twenty thousand matches the Chinese.
揚州大都督 is Grand Governor-General (大都督), not Protector General (都護); the repair corrects the office title.
名日簡 means he was named Rijian, not born Rijian; the repair fixes that naming verb without other changes.
鄆、齊 are Yun and Qi; 鄆 is Yun Prefecture, not Yan, and the repair restores the correct place name (context s0188 also has civilians fleeing into 鄆).
貸死 means commutation/sparing of the death penalty; 'lent death by pardon' is a nonsensical calque, and the repair states the clemency correctly.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0010/r0011 show English Li Yumou came only from fusing the verb 謀 into the name 李宇; the personal-name claim must read Li Yu while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
